full_judgment: 11. A reference to Order XXI, Rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure shows that when against any party a decree for injunction is passed and he has the opportunity of obeying the decree and he willfully failed to obey it, the decree may be enforced by detaining him in civil prison, or by the attachment of his property or by both. Thus it will be pertinent to consider whether the respondent had the opportunity to obey the decree and had willfully failed to obey the same. In this case, the appellant examined 3 witnesses and the respondent examined 4 witnesses. The learned trial Court considered the evidence of both the parties in extinction in the judgment wherein it was observed that after the passing of the order of temporary injunction in favour of the appellant there was a talk of compromise between the parties. The trial Court did not find any cogent reason to disbelieve this evidence and accepted the contention of the parties that there was a talk of compromise and solenama (Swaranlipi) was executed between the parties though not filed in the suit The trial Court also considered another material aspect that the suit land was recorded in the name of plaintiff's co-sharer and after the departure of the brother of the appellant, the respondent was in possession of 672 decimals of land in suit plot. The trial Court found that the respondent was already in possession before the declaration of the property as enemy property and as such the respondent did not willfully disobey the said order. Thus, the learned Munsif on consideration of evidence on record held that the respondent did not get any opportunity to disobey the decree for permanent injunction and in fact there was no willful disobedience of the order of the Court. This factual determination of the issue was affirmed by the learned Single Judge. Thus there was no apparent illegality in the impugned judgment.
